correctness.rationale: The finite graphs, neighborhoods, closed-walk quantifiers, label normalization, temporal and spatial equivalences are explicit. An exact per-start mask recurrence and an independent C++ recursive walk enumeration check every possible adjacent-vertex sequence through the claimed optimum for four fixed graphs. Independent Python DFS agrees on all rooted and temporal totals; every smaller even length has strictly deficient observed coverage. Bipartiteness forbids odd closed walks. Distance-preserving full automorphisms give exact 5+1+3+1 orbits, independently verified against representatives; both standalone programs executed from the final paths and printed ALL PASS.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary text defines MCDW, while published tree monitoring, block-intersection Steiner systems, graph automorphism classification and similarly named pursuit-evasion parameters do not imply the four-graph optimum cyclic route and ten-orbit classification. Actual bibliographic and named-graph searches found no equivalent or stronger coverage. A directly relevant 2016 multiplicity source is inaccessible, preventing a claim of absolute historical priority; recorded as residual risk rather than falsely stated not covering.
residual_risks: The primary full text of Dyer and Howell (2016), The multiplicity of watchman’s walks, Congressus Numerantium 226:301–317, was not available after arXiv/open-access searches. It could contain a stronger classification or a special case.
Unindexed small-graph computations may exist, and topic or subject classification cannot establish publication priority.
The 2008 date is a day-resolved public workshop presentation of the graph class, not the first date of every historical watchman paper; no speculative date was inserted.

value.rationale: The four graphs form a precisely motivated exceptional quartet in the cubic symmetric girth-six classification. The full patrol optimization and exact temporal/spatial orbit census is a natural complete finite classification, exposing qualitatively different patrol supports: a doubled tree, cycle-plus-excursions, and genuinely simple dominating cycles. These sharp distinctions are not determined by ordinary dominating sets or symmetry orders alone and provide reusable benchmark cases for static patrol design. The claim requires no unproved downstream application.
